levelIntroduction.title: Welcome to Loop Land! 🔄
levelIntroduction.description: Loops are like doing something over and over again! Just like when you count to 10 or brush each tooth. In code, loops help us repeat actions without writing the same thing many times.

concepts.name: What is a Loop?
concepts.explanation: A loop repeats code multiple times. Instead of writing the same code 10 times, we can use a loop to do it automatically!

concepts.name: Loop Counter
concepts.explanation: Most loops use a counter variable that changes each time. This helps the loop know when to stop.

concepts.name: Stopping the Loop
concepts.explanation: Every loop needs a way to stop! We use conditions like 'count < 10' to tell the loop when to finish.

levelIntroduction.readyMessage: Ready to help our ghost fix some loopy code? Let's go!

challenges.title: The Infinite Haunting
challenges.description: Oh no! This loop never stops haunting! The ghost is stuck saying 'Boo!' forever. Can you help fix the loop so it stops after 5 times?
hints: The loop needs to change something to eventually stop...
What variable controls when the loop ends? It's 'count'!
Try adding 'count++' after the console.log to make count go up each time!
challenges.educationalContent: Loops need a way to eventually stop. We use a counter variable and increment it (make it bigger) each time through the loop. Without incrementing, the loop runs forever!

challenges.title: The Wrong Direction Ghost
challenges.description: This ghost is counting backwards when it should count forwards! Help fix the loop so it counts from 1 to 3.
hints: Look at where the loop starts and which direction it goes...
The loop should start at 1 and go UP to 3, not down from 3!
challenges.educationalContent: For loops have three parts: where to start, when to stop, and how to change. We can count up (i++) or down (i--), but we need to make sure all three parts work together!

challenges.title: The Off-By-One Ghost
challenges.description: This ghost wants to haunt 10 houses, but the loop only visits 9! Can you fix it?
hints: Count on your fingers: does 'house < 10' include 10?
The symbol '<' means 'less than', so it stops BEFORE 10!
Change '<' to '<=' which means 'less than or equal to' - that includes 10!
challenges.educationalContent: The difference between < and <= is important! '<' means 'less than' (stops before), while '<=' means 'less than or equal to' (includes the number). This is called an 'off-by-one' error.

challenges.title: The Nested Ghost Party
challenges.description: The ghost wants to invite 3 friends and give each friend 2 treats. But something's wrong with the inner loop!
hints: Each friend should get 2 treats, but they're only getting 1!
Look at the inner loop condition - does 'treat < 2' give 2 treats?
Change '<' to '<=' so the loop includes treat number 2!
challenges.educationalContent: Nested loops are loops inside loops! The inner loop runs completely for each time the outer loop runs. If the outer loop runs 3 times and the inner loop runs 2 times, we get 3 × 2 = 6 total actions!
